stem: A trader can spend at most Rs 12,000 on two types of goods X and Y. Type X costs Rs 200 per unit and type Y costs Rs 300 per unit. He must buy at least 10 units of X and at least 20 units of Y. He earns Rs 50 profit per unit of X and Rs 60 per unit of Y. Which combination gives him the maximum profit within his budget?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Budget: 2000+6000=8000<=12000. Profit: 500+1200=1700. Feasible minimum corner but far from maximum.

explanation: Check feasibility (budget <= 12000, x >= 10, y >= 20) for each option, then compare profits. All four options are feasible; option 1 gives the highest profit of Rs 2700.

explanation_sections.punchline: Among feasible options, maximum profit goes to the combination that best exploits the remaining budget after satisfying minimum requirements.
explanation_sections.approach: For each option: verify 200x+300y<=12000, x>=10, y>=20. Then compute 50x+60y. Results: option1->2700, option2->2300, option3->1700, option4->2500. Pick 2700.
explanation_sections.lesson: In bounded LPP word problems, always check all constraints before comparing objectives. Spending the full budget does not guarantee maximum profit.
explanation_sections.timing: 90 s. Fastest route: compute profits first (option 3 obviously low), check feasibility of top two.
